subject: Post-call: Evexis Health — data-privacy & logging requirements (recap + next steps)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Brian O'Connell <b.oconnell@evexishealth.com>, Anna Park <anna.park@evexishealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Evexis Health — data-privacy & logging requirements (recap + next steps)

Hi Brian / Anna — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps. I'll keep this tight and flag the bits our security/tech teams call out as blockers so we can address them in the follow-up call.

Key pain points you shared:
- Need to avoid persistent PII storage in application-level inference logs (names, SSNs, medical identifiers).
- Regulatory retention windows vary by dataset (some clinical notes require 7+ years; others should be deleted after 30–90 days).
- Need cryptographic protections for audit logs and proof of deletion for compliance audits.
- Need full traceability for who/what asked for an inference (user id, app id, timestamp), but with PII redaction before long-term storage.

Current stack summary you gave:
- App hosted in AWS (us-west-2), proprietary EHR integration, primary data processing in their VPC.
- Existing logging uses CloudWatch + S3 lifecycle rules; security team wants more granular control over inference-level logs.

Success criteria you listed:
- Demonstrate a deployment (Private or Dedicated) that never persists raw PII in the long-term logs.
- Provide retention policies and a tamper-evident audit trail for token-level billing and request provenance.
- Satisfy initial evidence requests for security review (SOC 2 summary, sample sanitized logs).

What Redwood can commit to (high level):
- Review of our default logging flows and a redaction checklist speciﬁc to inference traces.
- Delivery of sample sanitized logs and a short SOC2 controls summary (attached).
- Technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (Monica) to map out a redaction + retention design in your VPC/Dedicated deployment.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll share the SOC2 summary and a sample sanitized log extract (attached).
2) Schedule a technical call next week (Monica + Priyom + Evexis security) to walk the redaction pipeline and retention controls.
3) Draft a mutually agreed M.A.P. (mutual action plan) with timelines for proof-of-concept (PoC) and security evidence delivery.

Would Tuesday 8/18 or Wednesday 8/19 afternoon PT work for a 60-minute technical session? Please confirm preferred time and any additional attendees from security/compliance.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_Summary_Excerpt.pdf (summary, 3 pages)
Attachment: sample_redaction_pipeline_logs.txt (sample of sanitized logs, PII redacted)

From: Brian O'Connell <b.oconnell@evexishealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Park <anna.park@evexishealth.com>, security@evexishealth.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Evexis Health — data-privacy & logging requirements (recap + next steps)

Thanks Rafael — helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our security team after a quick read: 

1) When you say "redaction before long-term storage," do you support configurable redaction at the token level (PII pattern removal) as part of the inference path, or would that be an external pre/post-processor? We need assurance that raw prompt payloads containing PHI never reach durable storage.

2) For audit logs we need a tamper-evident chain (hashed entries and rotation of keys). Is that supported out-of-the-box in Dedicated/Private deployments or is that a custom integration with our KMS/HSM?

3) Our legal team also wants a clear retention SLA for inference logs (time-to-delete + proof). Can you provide an expected retention enforcement mechanism?

We can do Tuesday 8/18 at 1:00pm PT for the tech session. I'll invite our security engineer (Maya Singh) and our infra lead (Tom Reyes).

-Brian

On a separate note: please send any non-sensitive sample logs now so our security team can preview them before the call.

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Brian O'Connell <b.oconnell@evexishealth.com>, Anna Park <anna.park@evexishealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 08:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Evexis Health — data-privacy & logging requirements (recap + next steps)

Appreciate the questions — high-level answers below and attaching the sample artifacts you requested. Monica and Priyom will go deeper on the tech call.

1) Token-level redaction: Redwood can run redaction as an inline step in the inference request pipeline (configurable regex + ML detectors). For Dedicated/Private we can ensure the inline redaction runs before any persistent logging; for Hosted we'd need to validate policy changes. The attached sample shows entries where names and patient ids were replaced with "<REDACTED>" before storage.

2) Tamper-evident audit trail: We support writing audit digests to an append-only store and can integrate with your KMS for signing keys. For Private deployments customers can supply their KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we offer an option to integrate customer-managed KMS. We'll enumerate the control points in the tech session.

3) Retention enforcement: We offer lifecycle enforcement hooks tied to S3 lifecycle or your object store APIs; for Private deployments we can call your purge APIs directly and provide a signed deletion certificate. Standard configs: 30, 90, 365 days; custom windows available as part of the PoC.

Attachments included now: Redwood_SOC2_Summary_Excerpt.pdf, sample_redaction_pipeline_logs.txt, mutual-action-plan-evexis-rdw-v1.docx

Confirming the tech session: Tue 2026-08-18, 13:00 PT. Monica, Priyom, please join. Brian / Evexis: feel free to add our pre-read (I've added a short playbook link in related_links).

Cheers, Rafael
